name: Swift
certifications: App Development with Swift Certified User (Apple and Certiport)
App Development with Swift Associate (Apple and Certiport)

beginner.summary: For developers who already program in another language such as Python, Java, C#, JavaScript or C++ and are new to Swift as a language, not to iOS app building. Covers installing the Swift toolchain with Swiftly, SwiftPM and the REPL, values and core types, strings and Unicode, control flow, functions, optionals, collections, enums and pattern matching, structs versus classes, properties, protocols and extensions, generic functions, error handling, ARC, modules and access control, closures and lazy sequences, Codable, Swift Testing, command-line tools, and a log-analyser capstone.
prerequisites: Writes working programs in at least one other language such as Python, Java, C#, JavaScript or C++
Uses a terminal confidently: running commands, setting environment variables and reading exit codes
Has a macOS, Linux or Windows machine with permission to install the Swift toolchain and an editor such as Visual Studio Code or Xcode
outcomes: Install and manage Swift toolchains and build, run, test and document packages with SwiftPM
Model data with structs, enums, classes, protocols and generics and explain value versus reference semantics
Handle absence and failure safely with optionals, throws, Result and the type system instead of sentinel values
Build and test a command-line tool that parses arguments, reads files, decodes JSON and exits with correct status codes

intermediate.summary: For developers who write everyday Swift and want to use the modern language properly. Covers async/await and structured concurrency, actors and global actors, Sendable and Swift 6 data-race safety, AsyncSequence, protocol-oriented design with some and any, generics with associated types and parameter packs, property wrappers and result builders, typed throws, collection performance, SwiftPM manifests, plugins and resources, Swift Testing in depth, Foundation formatting, Regex, key paths, using macros, logging, async networking, Linux and Docker builds, and a concurrent indexing library capstone.
prerequisites: Completed the beginner Swift level or can write structs, enums, protocols, generics, closures and throwing functions without help
Can create, build and test a SwiftPM package from the command line
Has Swift 6.x installed on macOS, Linux or Windows and Docker available for the Linux day
outcomes: Write data-race-free concurrent code with async/await, task groups, actors and Sendable under the Swift 6 language mode
Design protocol-based APIs with generics, opaque and existential types and typed errors
Structure multi-target SwiftPM packages with plugins, resources and a thorough Swift Testing suite
Build and ship a Swift library that runs on macOS and Linux with logging, networking and cross-compiled output

objectives: Write async code with structured concurrency

advanced.summary: For experienced Swift engineers who build libraries, services and tooling. Covers ownership with noncopyable types, Span and InlineArray, writing macros with swift-syntax, executors and isolation inheritance, Mutex and Atomic, migrating code to Swift 6, generics internals and performance profiling, C, C++, Objective-C and Java interop, server-side Swift with Hummingbird, SwiftNIO, PostgresNIO, OpenAPI and gRPC, observability, Embedded Swift and WebAssembly, library evolution, one SwiftUI data-flow day, supply-chain release engineering, and a multi-package capstone.
prerequisites: Completed the intermediate Swift level or writes actors, task groups, generics and SwiftPM packages routinely
Can read compiler diagnostics and profile with Instruments, perf or valgrind
Has Swift 6.x on macOS or Linux, Docker and a PostgreSQL instance available for the server days
outcomes: Use ownership, noncopyable types, Span, Mutex and Atomic to write predictable low-level Swift
Write macros, plan Swift 6 migrations and evolve public library APIs without breaking clients
Integrate Swift with C, C++, Objective-C and Java and run it on servers, Embedded targets and WebAssembly
Build, observe and ship a production Swift service with SwiftNIO, Hummingbird, OpenAPI and PostgreSQL
